The Scheitholt is a traditional German chordophone of the drone-zither family, and is also regarded as the ancestor of the modern zither. The early form was a wooden resonating box about 50 cm long and 5 cm wide, with a simple head and two or three strings of brass, animal hair, gut or waxed hemp; there was no fretboard, and metal wires set into the wood served as frets. It is played flat on a table or on the lap: the left hand stops the strings with a wooden rod and the right hand plucks with thumb and index finger, or with a pick of horn, wood or goose quill. Some strings serve as drones. It was still found in the Alps, southern and northern Germany, the Saxon Erzgebirge and Upper Lusatia in the nineteenth century.
夏侯特為傳統德國弦鳴樂器，屬持續音齊特琴，可能源自古希臘單弦琴；名稱原指劈柴木段: The Scheitholt is a traditional German chordophone of the drone-zither type, possibly descended from the ancient Greek monochord; the name first meant a split log, was applied to this instrument from the sixteenth century, and was famously described by Praetorius in 1619. It can be traced to Bavaria-Austria in the fourteenth century, and is called hummel in northern Germany. Similar instruments are found in the Nordic countries; the Scheitholt was probably carried to Pennsylvania by German immigrants and evolved into the Appalachian dulcimer in the late eighteenth century. In the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries the number of strings rose to three or four, the soundbox grew and a fretboard was added; in the mid-eighteenth century the kratzzither or scherrzither branched off, and in the nineteenth century the instrument was still in use in the Alps, northern and southern Germany, the Erzgebirge and Upper Lusatia.
夏侯特為木製弦鳴樂器，原始共鳴箱約長五十公分、寬五公分，早期無指板，以金屬線嵌入: The Scheitholt is a wooden chordophone; the original resonating box is about 50 cm long and 5 cm wide. Early instruments had no fretboard and used metal wires set into the wood as frets; later the box grew larger and a separate fretboard was glued on. The strings could be brass, or animal hair, gut or waxed hemp. It is played with a wooden sliding rod stopping the strings and plucking directly, or with picks of horn or wood or a goose-quill tube. The materials of the remaining parts are not stated.
演奏夏侯特時，先將琴身水平置於桌面或演奏者膝上。左手以木製滑棒按壓琴弦，右手拇指: To play the Scheitholt, first lay the instrument flat on a table or on your lap. The left hand stops the strings with a wooden sliding rod; the right thumb and index finger can pluck directly, or you can use a horn or wooden pick or a goose-quill tube. Some strings carry the drone, so a beginner should first settle the angle at which the instrument is held, then practise stopping and plucking together, and keep the drone unbroken while the melody moves.
謝特霍爾特琴音色溫潤而清透，具有明亮的金屬質感，兼具古樸的鄉土韻味。其音域屬於中: The Scheitholt's timbre is warm and clear, with a bright metallic sheen and an old rustic flavour. Its range lies in the upper-middle register, and the notes are clear and penetrating. A struck string resonates well, and the wooden soundbox amplifies it into a warm sound that is not harsh. Compared with the modern yangqin (dulcimer) the Scheitholt sounds warmer and more inward, without the dulcimer's brightness and edge; compared with the harp, its tone is coarser and more folk-flavoured. The sound decays at a moderate rate, which gives the playing its own sense of rhythm and swing and suits folk tunes and traditional pieces.
